subject.title: [Bug]: gpt-5.3-codex-spark emits empty arguments for required tool calls

question: Should OpenClaw support `gpt-5.3-codex-spark` when an account catalog exposes it but the user explicitly selects the embedded `openclaw` runtime, or should that combination fail clearly in favor of the native Codex runtime?
rationale: Current docs establish that explicit embedded-runtime selection is generally supported while Spark remains catalog-limited; deciding whether this exact runtime/model combination is a supported product contract is necessary before changing provider behavior.

options.title: Support the embedded runtime
options.body: Require a redacted raw trace and repair provider-side argument normalization if OpenClaw drops valid upstream argument data.

options.title: Restrict Spark to native Codex
options.body: Document and enforce a clear configuration error when Spark is selected with the embedded OpenClaw runtime.

recommendation.title: Support the embedded runtime
recommendation.body: Require a redacted raw trace and repair provider-side argument normalization if OpenClaw drops valid upstream argument data.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work connects this owner to the OpenAI Codex provider and model-catalog boundary that must define the supported route.
